title: Validate analyzer startup, reap dead helpers, single-flight the registry
description:
Nothing supervises the Dart analyzer child. Three concrete defects:

1. src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj:38-51 -- start! reads the banner with
   (edn/read {:eof nil} out) and returns the record regardless. A helper that
   died during `dart run` yields :banner nil and nobody looks.

2. src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj:98-104 -- for-root respawns on EVERY request
   once the child is dead, and each respawn is a fresh `dart run` compile
   (~3s). A missing/broken `dart` therefore means a new compile per mouse move.

3. Same lines -- the dead analyzer is never stop!ed. swap! assoc drops the
   reference; the Process object, reader, writer (and babashka.process's reaper)
   linger until GC. If the OS process already exited this leaks local objects
   rather than a running process, but stop! before replacement is still correct.

Note: the Node RESTART_LIMIT (extension/client.js:12,41) is NOT the fix and was
never defeated -- it correctly supervises Node -> Babashka. Resetting failures
on any successful round trip (client.js:119) is right, because the bb daemon is
demonstrably alive. The gap is purely Babashka -> Dart.

Work:
  - Require a valid startup banner; treat nil/EOF as a failed start.
  - stop! the previous analyzer before replacing it in the registry.
  - Make for-root single-flight. CAUTION: the obvious `swap!` with start! inside
    is a trap -- swap! retries under contention and would spawn duplicate Dart
    processes. Use a lock on the registry or a per-root promise/delay.
  - Per-root failure count with backoff so a broken `dart` cannot respawn on
    every request.

Acceptance: killing the helper mid-session produces at most one respawn attempt
per backoff window, not one per request; a helper that fails to start surfaces
an error instead of a silently broken analyzer record.
close_reason:
Registry rewritten as root -> {:delay :failures :created-at}.

- start! validates the banner: a non-map/EOF banner kills the child and throws with the exact `dart run` command to try by hand.
- The spawn lives inside a per-root delay, so swap! retries cannot duplicate it; concurrent first use shares one `dart run` (test asserts 8 threads -> 1 spawn).
- The displaced analyzer is stop!ed by whichever thread won the CAS that replaced it, and stop! now closes stdout as well as stdin before destroy-tree.
- Backoff 0/1s/2s/4s...60s per root, keyed off consecutive bad starts. A helper that served >=30s before dying is not counted as a failure, so an ordinary kill gets an immediate restart; a start that throws or a helper that dies young does.
- for-root throws instead of returning a broken record; daemon.clj turns that into a JSON-RPC error and extension.js already logs it.

New test/registry_test.clj (bb task test:registry, no Dart needed) stubs start!/alive?/stop! and covers reuse, single-flight, reaping, both backoff paths, window expiry, and shutdown/cache upkeep over a failed entry. Verified live too: with a bogus CLJD_RESOLVE_HELPER, 3 requests cost 2 dart invocations. test:parse, test:registry, test:extension, test:analyzer, test:resolve all green.

Closed ahead of its cljd-resolve-1sf.1 dependency (--force): the fixture/CI work is still open, but test:registry needs no Dart and no fixture and gives this change its own regression net.

Follow-up filed as cljd-resolve-1sf.12 (the banner read itself still has no deadline).

title: Analyzer request deadline with generation-safe eviction and backoff
description:
src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj:61 -- ask! blocks in edn/read with no deadline.
Narrower than it first looks: a DEAD process returns nil at EOF. But a
live-but-wedged helper hangs forever, and because the daemon is single-threaded
(src/cljd_resolve/daemon.clj:131 serve loop) that wedges everything until the
user restarts by hand.

The timeout path is not a small wrapper around edn/read -- a blocking stream
read cannot be interrupted directly. Required sequence:

  1. Mark that analyzer GENERATION unhealthy.
  2. Evict from the registry ONLY if it is still the current generation.
     Without this, a request that unwinds late evicts or destroys the
     replacement analyzer that was created after it timed out.
  3. Close stdin/stdout and destroy the child -- that is what unwinds the
     blocked read.
  4. Apply the backoff from the startup issue before another process starts.

Implementation sketch: run ask! in a future, deref with timeout; on timeout
destroy the process so the blocked thread unwinds and dies. Note the blocked
thread still holds (:lock a), so eviction from the registry is what lets the
next request make progress.

Acceptance: a deliberately wedged helper causes one request to fail with a
timeout and the NEXT request to succeed against a fresh analyzer, with no
possibility of the timed-out request killing that replacement.

title: Deduplicate in-flight resolves with per-caller cancellation
description:
The hover and definition providers each call resolveAt independently
(extension/extension.js:144 and :156, both hitting :115), so the same cursor
position costs two full round trips including two copies of the whole document
text. README.md also claims -- wrongly -- that both are answered "from a single
resolve call"; fix that line too.

Share the in-flight promise, keyed on {file, text, line, character}.

CRITICAL correctness detail: do NOT attach the first caller's cancellation token
to the shared transport request. If the hover cancels while definition is still
waiting on the same result, the shared promise resolves to null and BOTH lose
it. Correct structure:

  - the shared underlying request carries NO token and is never cancelled
    (the daemon does the work regardless; cancellation was only ever a
    client-side discard)
  - each consumer independently races that shared promise against its own token
  - the map entry is removed in a `finally`

Acceptance: a test where consumer A cancels and consumer B still receives the
resolved value.

title: Chunk warm-up client-side so hovers interleave
description:
warmUp resolves every library in one request (src/cljd_resolve/daemon.clj:110-117,
`(run! #(an/library? a %) libs)`), takes ~8s, is allowed 120s by the client
(extension/extension.js:188), and runs in the same sequential serve loop as
every hover. So every hover on file-open queues behind the whole batch. This is
not a rapid-cursor hypothetical; it happens on every file open.

REJECTED APPROACH: moving warmUp to a future. It buys a few seconds once per
project and costs a shared writer + lock, tracked background tasks, shutdown and
clearCache coordination, and a single-flight registry as a prerequisite. That is
the largest and riskiest change in the plan for the smallest window.

ADOPTED: let the CLIENT do the chunking. One library per warmUp request, each
awaited by the Node client. The serve loop reads stdin line by line, so a hover
sent while chunk N is in flight is simply the next line read -- interleaving
falls out of the existing sequential design, with zero concurrency in the daemon.

Split the analyzer start into its own chunk so the `dart run` compile is its own
unit. Worst-case hover latency during warm-up then becomes:
  ~3s   analyzer start chunk
  ~5.5s first Flutter SDK library
  ~10ms every library after

instead of the whole batch.

Work:
  - Daemon: a method that starts the analyzer only, and a per-library warm-up
    method (or warmUp taking a single lib). Keep returning the lib list so the
    client knows what to iterate.
  - Client: fetch the lib list, then await one request per library.
  - The Node client is already id-keyed (extension/client.js:115), so nothing
    there assumes ordering.

Acceptance: a hover issued during warm-up is answered within one chunk, not
after the full batch.

title: Portable test fixtures and CI
description:
Both integration suites hardcode the author's machine:

  test/analyzer_test.clj:15  (or (first *command-line-args*) "/Users/gavin/code/vibe/cljd/hello")
  test/resolve_test.clj:14   same

So `bb test` does not run anywhere but here, and there is no CI at all
(no .github/).

This lands first on purpose: the supervision work that follows is the riskiest
refactor in the repository, and doing it with no runnable regression net on one
machine is backwards.

Work:
  - CLJD_TEST_PROJECT env override, falling back to a checked-in fixture rather
    than an absolute path.
  - Small checked-in Dart fixture project (pubspec + a lib file) sufficient for
    the analyzer/resolve suites. Flutter SDK tests stay a separate optional tier.
  - .github/workflows: run test:parse and test:extension on every push (neither
    needs Dart); gate test:analyzer and test:resolve behind the Flutter tier.

Acceptance: `bb test` passes on a clean checkout with no Flutter SDK, running
the two suites that do not need one, and CI is green.
close_reason: Integration suites now run against a target (test/cljd_resolve/test_target.clj): the checked-in Dart fixture in test/fixture by default, a real Flutter project via CLJD_TEST_PROJECT/CLJD_TEST_TARGET. No absolute paths left; dart pub get is self-healing; missing SDK is a SKIP unless CLJD_TEST_STRICT=1. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs core+fixture tiers on every push, flutter tier weekly/on-demand.

title: Harden cljd-resolve before adding features
description:
Hardening pass on the cljd-resolve prototype, derived from two external
reviews plus a verification pass against the code (2026-08-30).

The prototype works and the component boundaries are sound. What is missing is
supervision of the Dart analyzer child process, a few correctness gaps in
caching and signature rendering, and the distribution/CI story.

Ordering principle: portable tests and CI land FIRST, because items 2 and 3 are
the riskiest refactor in the repo (process lifecycle, eviction races, backoff)
and today the only tests that would catch a regression in them are hardcoded to
one machine.

Explicitly OUT of scope, after review:
  - JSON-RPC capability negotiation. One client, same repo, no independent
    release. A plain version field is enough.
  - Making the depth-3 owner-candidate bound (parse.clj:194) configurable. It
    is a documented positional heuristic; the bound is what makes it terminate
    cheaply. A knob nobody tunes.
  - Threaded/async warm-up with a shared writer lock and tracked background
    tasks. Superseded by client-paced chunking -- see the warm-up issue.
  - Patching the vendored analyzer.dart to fix the whitespace protocol or the
    `import '${lib}'` interpolation. Both are upstream ClojureDart code
    (identical at vendor/analyzer.dart.upstream:437); fixing them there widens
    the vendored diff and worsens the upgrade burden. Validate on the Clojure
    side instead.

title: Startup banner read has no deadline
description:
src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj start! blocks in (edn/read out) waiting for the helper's banner with no deadline. A helper that neither exits nor answers -- a wedged `dart run`, a pub solve waiting on the network -- hangs the single-threaded daemon (daemon.clj serve loop) forever, and because the registry entry is an unforced delay every other caller for that root blocks on it too.

Not fixed by cljd-resolve-1sf.2, which only covers a helper that DIES (EOF -> throw) and the respawn storm that followed. Not fixed by cljd-resolve-1sf.3 either, whose deadline is around ask!.

Work: read the banner under a timeout (future + deref with timeout), and on expiry kill! the child so the blocked read unwinds, then fail the start so the existing backoff applies. Share the eviction/generation machinery with cljd-resolve-1sf.3 rather than growing a second one.

Acceptance: a helper that never writes a banner fails the start within the deadline instead of wedging the daemon, and the next request is backed off rather than spawning again.

title: Make the VSCode package self-contained and declare platform support
description:
A normal .vsix built from extension/ would not be self-contained.

  - extension/.vscodeignore is two lines (.vscode/**, **/*.map). Nothing
    assembles bin/, src/, bb.edn or helper/ into the package.
  - extension/extension.js:49 -- daemonPath's first candidate is
    <extensionPath>/bin/cljd-resolve, commented "packaged alongside". No build
    step produces that. It is a dead branch today.
  - bin/cljd-resolve is a POSIX sh script, but extension/package.json declares
    no platform restriction, so the marketplace would offer it on Windows.

Work (either direction is acceptable, pick one):
  A. A packaging task that assembles a self-contained extension directory, which
     makes the daemonPath branch real; or
  B. Delete the dead branch, document the symlink-into-the-repo install as the
     only supported one, and say so in the README.

Either way, declare the platform support in package.json rather than leaving it
implicit.

title: Signature fidelity: restore required, render function types
description:
Hovers show Dart declarations that would not compile.

(a) `required` is dropped. helper/bin/analyzer.dart:255 has
    `//':required': p.isRequired` commented out. For Flutter constructors that
    is most named parameters.

    This is a ONE-LINE uncomment: M() already drops false values
    (helper/bin/analyzer.dart:22, `if (v == null || v == false || ...) return;`),
    so non-required parameters emit nothing and the payload does not grow.
    Then render it in src/cljd_resolve/render.clj (param-str / params-str).

(b) Function-typed parameters collapse to bare `Function`. The helper ALREADY
    emits the full structure -- helper/bin/analyzer.dart:141 FunctionType emits
    :return-type, :parameters and :type-parameters. The loss is entirely in
    src/cljd_resolve/render.clj:7 type-str, which reads :element-name "Function"
    and stops.

    Worse than lossy: type-str then appends :type-parameters as if they were
    type ARGUMENTS, so a generic callback renders `Function<T>` -- which is
    wrong, not merely incomplete. For a FunctionType those are the generic type
    formals and belong before the parameter list.

    So this is render-side only. Tests needed for nested callbacks, nullability
    (`void Function()?`), and generic function types.

Acceptance: a Flutter constructor hover shows `required` on the parameters that
have it, and a callback parameter renders its real signature rather than
`Function` or `Function<T>`.

title: line-index cache grows without bound
description:
src/cljd_resolve/daemon.clj:43-51 -- line-index-cache keys on
[path lastModified length], so every save of a file adds a NEW permanent entry
and the old one is never evicted. Correctness is fine (a stale key is never hit
again); it is a pure unbounded leak in a long-running daemon.

Fix: key on the path alone, store [stamp idx] as the value so a changed file
replaces its entry rather than appending a new one.

Acceptance: editing and saving the same file N times leaves one entry, not N.

title: Skip the material_ui tier when the project lacks the library
description:
`bb test:material-ui` pointed at a Flutter project that does not depend on material_ui produces ~25 opaque FAILs (every `elt` returns nil) instead of the SKIP the target machinery gives for a missing SDK or project. test_target.clj's design intent is that a target which cannot run is a skip; a target whose :lib does not resolve in the chosen project cannot run.

Fix: have begin! probe the target's :lib once (`lib <uri>` against the helper, or cljd-resolve.analyzer/library?) and turn a false answer into {:skip "..."}. Note test_target.clj deliberately has no analyzer dependency today, and resolve_test drives the daemon as a subprocess, so this costs one extra `dart run` per suite -- weigh that against the failure being legible.

Not urgent: CI adds material_ui to its throwaway app explicitly, and stable Flutter is already past the >=3.44 that material_ui requires.

title: Document the vendored analyzer upgrade process
description:
The vendored helper is pinned to analyzer 6.4.1 and ClojureDart commit 01c41592
with no documented upgrade path. Fine for a spike; needs a process before this
becomes long-lived infrastructure.

Wanted:
  - A compatibility note recording the pinned analyzer + ClojureDart versions
    and what breaks if they drift.
  - A test or task that diffs helper/bin/analyzer.dart against
    vendor/analyzer.dart.upstream and fails if the patch stops applying cleanly
    to a newer upstream. The patch is currently 120 diff lines, additive only,
    confined to doc/location emission -- keeping it that small IS the upgrade
    strategy, so a size/shape regression is worth catching.
  - A written procedure for pulling a new upstream analyzer.dart.

Lower priority than everything else in the epic, but recorded so the pin does
not quietly rot.

title: Protocol version, URI validation, and dead-code cleanup
description:
Small independent items, groupable into one pass.

1. Protocol version field. The daemon calls itself JSON-RPC 2.0 but supports a
   private subset and validates nothing. A `protocol` version in the ping/handshake
   response, checked by the client, prevents a stale packaged extension from
   silently mismatching a newer daemon. Deliberately NOT a capability
   negotiation -- one client, same repo, no independent release.

2. Library URI validation. Allow only well-formed dart: and package: URIs with
   no whitespace, quotes or control characters, before
   src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj:81 (library?) and :86 (element).

   Why here and not in the helper: the whitespace-delimited command protocol
   (helper/bin/analyzer.dart:500, `line.split(" ")`) and the
   `import '${lib}' as libalias;` interpolation are UPSTREAM ClojureDart code,
   unmodified by this project -- the interpolation is identical at
   vendor/analyzer.dart.upstream:437, and our whole patch is 120 diff lines
   confined to doc/location emission. Patching it there widens the vendored diff
   and worsens the upgrade burden.

   But inherited code is still this system's boundary: aliases come from the ns
   form of an UNSAVED workspace buffer, so a library string containing a space
   shifts tokens[1]/tokens[2] and corrupts the command. Validating before we
   send is this project's responsibility.

3. Dead code / doc cleanup:
   - src/cljd_resolve/resolve.clj:17-18 -- clojure.java.io and clojure.string
     are required but unused.
   - src/cljd_resolve/resolve.clj:98 -- `:as nsi` destructured but unused in
     resolve-dot-name.
   - README.md claims hover and definition are answered "from a single resolve
     call". They are not (see the dedup issue). Fix whichever the dedup work
     leaves untrue.

title: Mtime-validate cached elements from local project sources
description:
Analyzer results, including misses, live until the user runs clearCache
(src/cljd_resolve/analyzer.clj:73-79). Local Dart edits can leave definitions
and docs stale indefinitely.

Deliberately LAST and deliberately small. The cache holds package:flutter/... and
dart:... elements -- SDK and pub dependencies that do not change mid-session --
and local .dart is the rare case in a project whose whole premise is writing
.cljd. clearCache exists and is documented. Building file-watcher infrastructure
for this is not proportionate.

Targeted approach: on cache read, mtime-validate only entries whose element
resolves to a file inside the project root; leave SDK/pub entries session-cached.

This is NOT the five-line change an earlier draft of the plan claimed. Known
complications, in order of how much they hurt:

  1. Cached nil misses carry no :file, so they cannot be classified as local or
     SDK at all. Decisive. Simplest honest answer: do not cache misses for
     projects at all, or key misses separately with a short TTL. Decide before
     implementing.
  2. Deleted files -- .lastModified returns 0 for a missing file, which reads as
     "changed" forever and re-asks on every hover.
  3. Nested metadata. Note addMeta IS applied to the class map itself
     (helper/bin/analyzer.dart:286 and :355), so a class map does carry a
     top-level :file. The real gap is narrower: members declared in part files
     carry their own :file, and find-in-class returns the MEMBER, not the class.
  4. Path containment must be canonical-path based, not a string prefix.
  5. A benign race between checking mtime and replacing the entry (worst case a
     duplicate ask!).

Acceptance: editing a local .dart file in the project makes the next hover on
its symbols show the new doc/location without a manual clearCache -- or, if the
complications above make that not worth it, an explicit decision recorded here
to keep clearCache manual.
